This is intentional. A link in a training document should continue to show the instructions that were current when that document was written. People comparing an old procedure with today's procedure need to know which version they are reading, especially when the steps look nearly the same at first glance.

An archived page has a date below its title and cannot be edited. To find the current guide, use the blue Current version link at the top of the archived page. Staff answering a question should check whether a current version exists before sharing an archive link as advice.

{"source":"Your scanner may show a red light during its first minute after you connect it. During that first check, the light means it is checking the paper path; it does not, by itself, mean there is a jam. Leave the sheet out while the check runs, and wait for the light to turn white before loading paper. If the light stays red for more than two minutes, turn the scanner off, clear any paper from the slot, and start it again. Keep the first-minute light separate from a red light that appears while a sheet is moving.

If the light turns red only after a sheet enters, look at where the paper stopped. Remove the sheet by pulling it gently in the direction it was moving. Do not pull it backward through the rollers. After the sheet comes out, check for torn paper before trying another sheet. A scrap left in the path can make the next attempt look like the same problem, so take a moment to inspect the slot rather than feeding a new sheet immediately.

If the red light repeats after you have cleared the path and tried another sheet, a worn roller may be involved. Support can help confirm that possibility from a short video of the feed. The video is useful because it shows how the sheet moves just before the light changes; a still photo of the red light alone does not show that behavior. A repeated light is a reason to ask for help, not enough information on its own to say a roller definitely needs replacing.

There is no need to send a video of the documents you were trying to scan. A blank sheet is enough to show the feed behavior. Before recording, remove any paper with private information from the area in view. The goal is to show the scanner taking in a sheet and, if it happens again, the point where it stops.
